Sir,

Further communication received by Mr. Gordon
Campbell, U. S. Marshall for China, from the Immigration and
Naturalization Service of the U. S. Dept. of Labour, definitely
show that Rabin's claim to American citizenship is entirely
without foundation.

Immigration records show that Nathan Rabin alias
Rabinovitch was born in Kopul, Russia, on September 12th, 1909,
and that his father Mendel Rabinovitch was born in Dvinsk,
Latvia, formerly Russia. Rabinovitch resided in the U.S.A.
from April 1928 until his deportation on November 4th, 1932.

Rabin's antecedents were traced by Immigration
officials through his maternal aunt, Mrs. Eva Goorwitch,
residing Apartment No. 302, No. 1761 Seward Avenue, Detroit,
Michigan, U.S.A. Dr. Bella Rabinovitch, a sister of Rabin's
on being contacted, made a sworn statement to Immigration
officials, giving the aforementioned particulars of her
brother's antecedents. He left Seattle, Washington, U.S.A.,
per S.S. "Princess Alice" for Shanghai on November 14th, 1932.
He was accompanied by his aunt and uncle Eva, and Boris
Goorwitch, who apparently, subsequently returned to the U.S.A.,
and are now residing at the aforementioned address in Detroit.

FILE

D. I. Glover

was accompanied on that occasion by three Japanese

agent provocateur for the Japanese Special Service
Section. The memo was obtained from the U.S.
Consul General with whose permission I forward it
for information.

Shanghai, March 16, 1939.

The matter is presumed to be of interest to the U.S.
authorities, apart from its general political significance,
because it involves one Nathan Rakens (Nathan Rabin) who claims
U.S. citizenship and to have a U.S. passport. Rakens has been
around Shanghai for some years, has an unsavory reputation, and
at one time for a short while was nominal manager of The Little
Club on Bubbling Well Road.

On March 6 Rakens, who has an extensive acquaintance
among the "night-life" world of Shanghai, asked Ralph Lynn if
he could use one of the rooms at Lynn's studio for a meeting,
so he told Lynn, between some Chinese and Japanese who desired
that their meeting should be private. Rakens told Lynn that
the meeting would not last more than five minutes. Lynn
consented and at the time fixed Rakens arrived accompanied by
three Japanese and the four of them went to Lynn's living room.
At the time Lynn was conducting classes in the studio. He
noticed that Rakens seemed nervous and went out two or three
times, evidently looking for the Chinese who were expected. Two
hours passed but no Chinese arrived. Lynn, becoming suspicious
decided to investigate, and saw Rakens and the three Japanese
leaving the house, all with pistols in their hands; they went
away in a large limousine motor car but Lynn, being flustered,
failed to note its license number.

Lynn was advised not to mention the incident to anyone
until the U.S. authorities had time to investigate the matter,
and Lynn said he would not. Lynn formed the opinion that
Rakens and the Japanese had planned to lure some Chinese to
Lynn's apartment and perhaps kill him there, but the Chinese
did not come. Lynn can be found at the above address. He
probably knows where Rakens lives or can be found.

（副本）

上海，1939年3月16日。

此事除具有一般政治意义外，据信亦引起美国当局的关注，因为它涉及一名自称拥有美国公民身份并持有美国护照的内森·拉肯斯（Nathan Rakens，即内森·拉宾 Nathan Rabin）。拉肯斯在上海活动已有数年，名声不佳，曾短暂担任静安寺路“小俱乐部”（The Little Club）的名义经理。

3月6日，在上海“夜生活”圈中交游广阔的拉肯斯询问拉尔夫·林恩，是否可以使用其工作室的一间房间举行会议。他告诉林恩，与会者包括一些中国人和日本人，他们希望会议私下进行。拉肯斯向林恩表示，会议持续时间不会超过五分钟。林恩表示同意。在约定时间，拉肯斯携三名日本人抵达，四人进入林恩的客厅。当时林恩正在工作室授课。他注意到拉肯斯显得神情紧张，并两三次外出，显然是在寻找预期的中国人。两个小时过去了，但未见中国人到来。林恩心生疑窦，决定前去查看，只见拉肯斯和那三名日本人离开住所，手中均持手枪；他们乘坐一辆大型豪华轿车离去，但林恩因惊慌失措，未能记下车辆牌照号码。

有人建议林恩在美国当局有时间调查此事之前，不要向任何人提及此事，林恩表示他不会这样做。林恩认为，拉肯斯和日本人原计划诱骗某名中国人至林恩的公寓，并可能将其杀害，但该中国人并未出现。林恩可在上述地址找到。他可能知道拉肯斯的住址或下落。

On the 20th, March 1939, it was learned that
Rabin, alias Rabens, alias Raven, had on the 5th,
March 1939, endeavoured to persuade Mr. Ralph Lynn

entered a large limousine, but Lynn, being somewhat
flustered, failed to note the number of the car.

Enquiries have been made at H.M.'s Passport
Office regarding George Hashinoya alleged to be in
possession of a Canadian passport, but no record
of this individual could be found.

Since forwarding the last report no further
information has been obtained about Rabin, who
apparently fearing reprisals for his part in bringing

RESUME OF INVESTIGATIONS MADE CONCERNING
THE ACTIVITIES OF ONE, NATHAN RABIN.

On February 26, 1939, information was received
to the effect that a British subject, named H. H. GOFF,
was endeavouring to sell illegally one hundred "MAUSER"
automatic pistols and ammunition. Enquiries revealed
that Goff is in partnership with one, named "BRAN" or
"BRAND" in the Native Industry Co., Room No. 503, No.169

On March 1, 1939, a foreigner called at Police

RAVEN, who resided at No. 33, Lane No. 150, Tifeng Road,
(Tel. No. 23163) and was alleged to be employed by the
Japanese Secret Service, had commissioned him to find a
buyer for the undermentioned arms and ammunition :-

12 lbs. each, firing 500 rounds per
minute, complete with magazine and
20,000 rounds per gun @ $2,500.oo each.
Total $ 25,000.oo.

Rabin first proposed that he should interest

关于内森·拉宾（NATHAN RABIN）活动之调查摘要。

1939年2月26日，收到情报称，一名名为 H. H. 戈夫（GOFF）的英国臣民正试图非法出售一百支“毛瑟”（MAUSER）自动手枪及弹药。调查显示，戈夫与一名名为“布兰”（BRAN）或“布兰德”（BRAND）的人合伙经营位于圆明园路169号503室的“本土工业公司”（Native Industry Co.），电话10751。

1939年3月1日，一名外国人来到警察总局，称一名名为 N. 拉宾（RABIN，又名雷文 RAVEN）的男子，居住于提封路150弄33号（电话23163），据称为日本特务机关工作，委托他为下列武器和弹药寻找买家：

1) 10挺机枪，长50厘米，每挺重12磅，射速每分钟500发，配有弹匣，每挺配20,000发子弹，单价2,500.00美元。总计25,000.00美元。

2) 50支全尺寸毛瑟自动手枪（1936年型），每支配一个弹匣（20发）及250发子弹，单价260.00美元。总计13,000.00美元。

拉宾首次提出参与此交易是在1939年2月25日，双方于海军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.）外相遇时。

he mentioned to the informer that if he succeeded
in finding a buyer, he could communicate with him
(Rabin) either through Bran (Brand ?) at the Native

Japanese known as "GEORGE" (Tel. No. 41346), whom
the informer knew to be a member of the Japanese

Telephone No. 41346 is listed under the

. Subsequent meetings took place between

On one occasion during Bran's temporary

with Bran, warned the informer to be careful of
Rabin. Asked if he thought it was a bogus deal,
Goff stated that he had nothing whatever to do with

Enquiries made by detectives show that the
telephone number (23163) given by Rabin as his private
pages.zh:

交谈中，他向线人提及，若线人成功找到买家，可通过圆明园路“本土工业公司”的布兰（Brand?）或一名被称为“乔治”（GEORGE）的日本人（电话41346）与他（拉宾）联系。线人已知“乔治”是日本特务机关成员。

电话号码41346登记在“Y. KUWAHATA，海宁北路24弄18号”名下。

随后，线人与拉宾在海军青年会多次会面，后来线人又在圆明园路169号的办公室会见了布兰（?）。

有一次，趁布兰暂时离开办公室之际，与布兰共事的戈夫警告线人要提防拉宾。当被问及这是否是一桩虚假交易时，戈夫表示他与此事毫无关系，无法判断真假，但他对拉宾非常怀疑。不过，他能说明的是，布兰（?）曾向他保证，他手头有一些待售枪支。

侦探进行的调查显示，拉宾提供的私人

number, is listed under the name of "SANDY GUTTERMAN",
House No. 33, Lane No. 15C, Tifeng Road. Gutterman
incidentally is at present in the Phillipine Islands,
having left Shanghai after being involved in a
fraudulent narcotic deal.

From enquiries made at the U.S. Consulate
General, it was learned that Rabin's claim to American
citizenship is without foundation.

Acting upon the information obtained, the
police arranged for the informer to introduce a
Chinese detective to Rabin as a prospective buyer
at a meeting which was to take place at the Chocolate
Shop, Nanking Road. Consequently, at 9.45 a.m. on
March 2nd. 1939, the introduction was made. The
detective, who assumed the role of "middleman",
discussed the conditions to purchase the second
described consignment of arms, consisting of "Mauser"
pistols. Rabin then stated that the pistols did
not actually belong to him, and that he was only
acting for the owner who resided in the French
Concession. He stipulated that the purchase money
should be delivered to an address in the French
Concession, to which he would lead the detective, and
where if everything was satisfactory, the arms would be
delivered. The detective objected to this arrangement
and proposed the International Settlement, claiming
that it would be much safer for him under this condition.

电话号码（23163）登记在“桑迪·古特曼”（SANDY GUTTERMAN）名下，地址为提封路15C弄33号。顺便提及，古特曼目前身在菲律宾群岛，他在卷入一起欺诈性毒品交易后离开了上海。

经向美国总领事馆查询，得知拉宾声称拥有美国公民身份毫无根据。

根据所获情报，警方安排线人在南京路巧克力店（Chocolate Shop）举行的会面中，将一名华籍侦探作为潜在买家介绍给拉宾。因此，在1939年3月2日上午9时45分，双方进行了介绍。扮演“中间人”角色的侦探讨论了购买第二批军火（即“毛瑟”手枪）的条件。拉宾随即表示，这些手枪实际上并不属于他，他只是代表居住在法租界的货主行事。他规定，购货款需送至法租界的一个地址，他将带领侦探前往该处，若一切顺利，将在该处交付武器。侦探反对这一安排，并提出在公共租界进行交易，声称在此条件下对他而言更为安全。

This terminated the interview, but it was agreed to
meet the following morning at the same place. At
the time appointed, the informer and the Chinese
detective met Rabin. The latter stated that the
seller had agreed to the stipulation made by the
purchaser to the effect that the sale should be
effected in the International Settlement. The seller,
however, stipulated that the money, $13,000.00 in
notes, should be produced for inspection prior to the
delivery of the arms. The detective protested that
this would leave the buyer open to either being held
up and robbed or defrauded by some other means. Rabin
then stated that he would have to leave the matter in
abeyance until he had consulted the owner on this point.
A further meeting was arranged for 5:45 p.m.
the same day. The parties met at the Chocolate Shop
as arranged, and on this occasion, Rabin suggested that
in order to allay the detective's suspicion, he should
provide himself with bodyguards. They should proceed
by motor car to an address to which he would lead them.
On arrival, the owner of the pistols would inspect the
money whilst they were in the car. They would then
proceed to inspect the pistols, after which the transfer
would be effected. This concluded the meeting, but
they arranged to meet again at 10:15 a.m. on the 4th.
March 1939.
At the appointed time, they again met, when
pages.zh:

此次面谈至此结束，但双方同意次日上午在同一地点再次会面。在约定时间，线人和华籍侦探会见了拉宾。后者表示，卖方已同意买方提出的在公共租界完成交易的规定。然而，卖方规定，在交付武器之前，必须先出示13,000.00美元现钞以供查验。侦探抗议称，这将使买方面临被抢劫或以其他手段诈骗的风险。拉宾随后表示，在他就此点咨询货主之前，此事只能暂缓。
双方约定于当日下午5时45分再次会面。各方按约定在巧克力店见面，此次拉宾建议，为消除侦探的疑虑，侦探应配备保镖。他们应乘车前往由拉宾带领的地址。到达后，手枪货主将在车内查验钱款。随后他们将去查验手枪，之后完成交接。此次会面至此结束，但双方约定于1939年3月4日上午10时15分再次会面。
在约定时间，双方再次会面，此时

Rabin was informed by the detective that the suggestion
made the previous day was unacceptable to the buyer.
The detective stipulated that the arms be delivered to
a place to be designated by him, but this was refused.
A further meeting took place at 5:30 p.m.
March 4th. 1939, but as no satisfactory arrangement
could be arrived at, no further meetings were arranged.
At 8:45 p.m. 6.3.39, C.P.C.2018 on traffic
duty at the intersection of Avenue and Seymour Roads,
who was accompanied by a Mr. S.Abolnik, residing at
Apt. "C" 2, No.1248 Rue Lafayette, French Concession,
went to Bubbling Well Police Station, where they made
the following report :-
At about 8.35 p.m. 6.3.39 an unidentified
motor car was proceeding on Avenue Road from West to
East with another motor car of the "Nash" or "Buick"
type, S.M.C. No.5601, following behind. When about
five yards west of Seymour Road, motor car No.5601
stopped quickly with a screech of brakes. Immediately
following this, a man was heard to cry out, as if in
pain. Four Japanese in civilian clothing were then
seen to jump from the car, pick up a male Chinese from
the roadway and bundle him into the car. C.P.C.2018
observed that the Chinese was bleeding profusely from
the head, whilst Mr. Abolnik noticed that he was wearing
some sort of dark coloured long gown. The car was
stationary only a very short period, a matter of seconds,
before it was driven away in an easterly direction.
Neither the C.P.C. nor Mr. Abolnik saw pistols or other
pages.zh:

侦探告知拉宾，买方不接受前一天提出的建议。侦探规定武器需运送至由其指定的地点，但这一要求被拒绝。
1939年3月4日下午5时30分，双方再次会面，但因未能达成令人满意的安排，故未再安排后续会面。
1939年3月6日晚上8时45分，在爱文义路（Avenue Road）和西摩路（Seymour Road）交叉口执行交通任务的警员 C.P.C.2018，陪同居住在法租界霞飞路1248号C座2室的 S. 阿博尔尼克（S. Abolnik）先生，前往静安寺捕房，作出如下报告：
1939年3月6日晚上8时35分左右，一辆不明机动车沿爱文义路由西向东行驶，另一辆“纳什”（Nash）或“别克”（Buick）型机动车（工部局车牌号5601）紧随其后。当行驶至西摩路以西约五码处时，5601号车急刹车停下。紧接着，听到有人发出痛苦的叫喊声。随后看见四名身穿便服的日本人从车上跳下，从路面上抱起一名中国男子，并将其塞入车内。C.P.C.2018观察到该中国人头部大量出血，而阿博尔尼克先生注意到他身穿某种深色长袍。该车仅静止了极短时间，不过数秒，便向东驶离。C.P.C. 和阿博尔尼克先生均未看见手枪或其他

private motor car No. 5601, it was found to be in

resides at Lane 24, House 18, Haining Road.
Detectives attached to Bubbling Well
Station made enquiries and requested the assistance

Sgt. Matsumoto of the Japanese Consular

At 4.00 p.m. 7.3.39 D.S. Nagamune, attached to

At 9.30 a.m. 8.3.39 the car was

静安寺捕房的侦探进行了查询，并请求日本领事馆警察协助前往上述车辆登记车主的住所。

He was asked to meet Wong outside the "Weida" Hotel,

On leaving the hotel, Mr. Boisseree parted

Mr. Boisseree subsequently learned that the

From enquiries made at Wong's residence,

离开酒店时，Boisseree先生与王分道扬镳，但在此之前，他注意到王和另一名中国人同那名外国人一起乘坐一辆停在外面的牌照号为5601的汽车离去。

At 9 a.m. March 13th. 1939, the informer
called on Rabin at Apt. No. 611, Broadway Mansions,
to which he had removed, following the abduction of
Wong. The informer noted on glancing at a date
block, lying on a desk, that Rabin had noted an
appointment for 10 a.m. that morning with Colonel
Agaki, Chief of the Intelligence Service. He also
noticed that an auto. pistol was lying in a half
opened drawer. During the ensuing conversation,
the informer told Rabin that the "buyer" for the
"Mauser" pistols insisted that the guns be delivered
to an address which he would designate, and that he
on no account would agree to any other proposal as
to accompanying Rabin or any other individual to
unknown addresses. Rabin then suggested that the
"buyer" should meet him that evening in the lounge
of the "Cathay" Hotel, where they could talk over
the proposed transaction. This proposition was,
however, later vetoed on the grounds that it would
be unwise to jeopardise the safety of the Chinese
detective, who was acting as the "buyer", as by this
time, it was very apparent that Rabin was acting in
the capacity of "agent provocation" for the Japanese
Secret Service.

他说，当他在桥屋（Bridge House）被日本宪兵队拘留时，他与一名名为王的广东籍囚犯交谈，王称他在与一名外国人谈判军火交易时，与另一人一同被捕。他们先去了“伟达”酒店，然后被外国人开车带到赫德路（Hart Road），在那里许多日本人包围了汽车并将他们逮捕。

to pursuade Mr. RALPH LYNN ( British ), Proprietor

Japanese, who desired that their meeting should be
private. Lynn, consented and at the appointed time,

four of them went to Lynn's living room, where they
remained for about two hours. As no Chinese arrived

went to investigate. He was just in time to see Rabin

limousine, but Lynn, being somewhat flustered, failed
to note the number of the car.

据称，迈耶是一名靠汇款生活的人，是美国加利福尼亚州好莱坞著名电影制片商米高梅公司（Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer）的一位合伙人的兄弟。据说他每月领取或曾领取500.00美元。他参与过几桩可疑的商业活动，显然完全肆无忌惮。

在最初的日记中，署名者提到，本案线人称拉宾与迈耶有联系，但确切关系尚不清楚。这两人可能参与了从日军占领区运出物资的活动，而拉宾主要在促成与某些日本人的必要安排方面发挥了作用，从而使这成为可能。

自上一份日记发出以来，线人已在拉宾的公寓与其多次会面，拉宾仍急于不让“军火交易”落空，但鉴于对

The informer was instructed by Rabin that he in communicating

At about 2:45 p.m. on the 15th. March, 1930,
a Mr. Robert Read, a Reservist of the U.S.Navy,residing
at the Foreign Y.M.C.A., called on the undersigned when
he divulged the following information : -

He stated that at about 5:30 p.m. on the
6th. March, 1930, he was partaking of some light
refreshment at the American Ex-Service Men's Club, 186
Peking Road, when Rabin approached him and asked him
if he would like to go for a motor car drive with him.
Having nothing better to do, he consented, and Rabin
drove to Avenue Joffre, French Concession.

On nearing the Veida Hotel, Rabin suggested
that they should visit some friends of his. As they
alighted from the car, Mr. Read met Mr. O.Boisserie,
whom he knew casually. Mr. Boisserie stated that he
had come to the hotel at the request of a Chinese friend,
who had asked him to witness a business transaction. They
all entered the hotel together, and Rabin led Mr. Read
to a room situated either on the first or second floor.
He was surprised when Mr. Boisserie followed them.

朱守灵侦探督察（D.I. Chu Shou Ling）的危险，未再安排进一步会面。

1930年3月15日下午2时45分左右，居住在外侨青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）的美国海军后备役人员罗伯特·里德（Robert Read）先生拜访了署名者，并透露了以下信息：

他说，1930年3月6日下午5时30分左右，他正在北京路186号的美军退伍军人俱乐部（American Ex-Service Men's Club）享用茶点，拉宾走近他，问他是否愿意和他一起开车兜风。由于无事可做，他同意了，拉宾便开车前往法租界霞飞路。

接近伟达酒店时，拉宾建议去拜访他的一些朋友。下车时，里德先生遇到了他泛泛之交的O. Boisserie先生。Boisserie先生表示，他是应一位中国朋友的要求来到酒店的，该朋友请他见证一笔商业交易。他们一起进入酒店，拉宾带领里德先生来到位于一楼或二楼的一个房间。当Boisserie先生跟随他们时，他感到惊讶。

Entering the room, they met a number of
Chinese who at once started to discuss something in
Chinese which Mr. Read did not understand. He did
not quite know what to think of the matter until one
of the Chinese locked the door. He then became
alarmed and informed Rabin that he was leaving, but
as told that this was impossible until the transaction
was concluded. He was not told what kind of a
transaction was taking place, but saw the Chinese
counting a large sum of money.

As soon as the door was unlocked, Mr. Read
made his way downstairs and waited outside the entrance.

Rabin came out with two of the Chinese and
talked excitedly with them for a few minutes. They then
entered a motor car No.5601, which was parked at the kerb,
and Rabin drove off at a fast pace in a westerly direction.
Several other Chinese who were standing on the pavement
then entered a car which was parked immediately behind
Rabin's and drove off after him.

Mr. Read then spoke to Mr. Boisserie and
asked him what it all meant, but the latter could not
give him any more details, other than that he had been
asked by a Chinese friend to witness the paying over of
a large sum of money.

进入房间后，他们遇到了一些中国人，这些人立即开始用中文讨论某些事情，里德先生听不懂。直到其中一名中国人锁上门，他才大致明白是怎么回事。随后他感到惊慌，告诉拉宾他要离开，但被告知在交易完成之前这是不可能的。他未被告知正在进行何种交易，但看到中国人在清点一大笔钱。

门一打开，里德先生便下楼并在入口处外等候。

拉宾带着两名中国人出来，兴奋地与他们交谈了几分钟。随后他们进入了一辆停在路边的牌照号为5601的汽车，拉宾快速向西驶去。随后，站在人行道上的其他几名中国人也进入了一辆紧停在拉宾车后的汽车，尾随而去。

里德先生随后与Boisserie先生交谈，询问这一切是什么意思，但后者除了称他是应一位中国朋友之邀见证一大笔款项的支付外，无法提供更多细节。

The following morning, two male Chinese who
were accompanied by Mr. Boisserie, called on Mr. Read
at the Foreign Y.M.C.A. and asked him if he knew where
Mr. Wong was, as he had not returned to his home. On
Mr. Read stating that he did not know and explaining
how he came to be in Rabin's company, one of the Chinese
informed him that he intended to find Rabin, and shoot
him. With that the men left the room and Mr. Read
not knowing what to do, consulted Mr. Carol Aleott,
well known radio commentator, who advised him to see
the undersigned.

Mr. Read assured the undersigned that what he
had stated was absolutely true, and that he knew nothing
of Rabin's intentions.

He further stated that as a Naval Reservist,
drawing a pension of U.S. $.$184.00 per month, he was
afraid that should the American Authorities hear of this
incident, he would possibly be deprived of his pension,
a very serious matter for a man of 47 years of age. The
undersigned is convinced that Mr. Read's story is true,
otherwise he would not have divulged the above information
to the Police, as Mr. Boisserie knowing of Mr. Read's
plight, took care not to mention his name either to
detectives attached to D'Veil or the French Police, when

次日早晨，两名由布瓦瑟里先生（Mr. Boisserie）陪同的中国男子前往基督教青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）拜访里德先生（Mr. Read），询问他是否知道黄先生（Mr. Wong）的下落，因为黄先生尚未回家。里德先生表示不知情，并解释了他是如何与拉宾（Rabin）结识的，其中一名中国男子随即告知他，自己打算找到拉宾并将其枪杀。随后这些人离开了房间，里德先生不知如何是好，便咨询了知名广播评论员卡罗尔·阿尔科特先生（Mr. Carol Aleott），后者建议他去见下文签署人。

里德先生向签署人保证，他所陈述的内容完全属实，且他对拉宾的意图一无所知。

他还表示，作为一名海军后备役人员，每月领取 184.00 美元的养老金，他担心如果美国当局得知此事，他可能会被剥夺养老金，这对于一位 47 岁的男子来说是一件非常严重的事情。签署人确信里德先生的故事是真实的，否则他不会向警方透露上述信息，因为布瓦瑟里先生深知里德先生的困境，在

should any action be taken against Rabin. In view

brought to the knowledge of the American Authorities.

similar case (C.l Misc.29/39) were in the custody of
the French Police, Mr. Read accompanied the undersigned
to Lukawei Station, where an identification parade was
held, but he could not identify any of the persons
paraded before him.

With the assistance of Det.Sgt. Yankovsky
of the French Police, the "Veida Hotel" was visited.
The 1st. and 2nd. floors were visited but Mr.
Read could not definitely point out the room where the

informed the undersigned that a prisoner, named Tsen Yah
Vung (周学文), arrested in connection with C.l Misc. No.
29/39, who had recently been returned by the Japanese
Gendarmerie after having been in their custody for three
days, had made the following statement to him :-

He stated that whilst he was in the custody

他表示，当他在

The following day, a man whom he subsequently

Tseu Yah Vung (周毓文) on being shown a

Tilton attached to B'Well, informed the undersigned

attached to C.I met a French citizen named Victor
Martin, who informed him that during the early morning

"Winter Gardens".

Rabin, who was armed, and under the influence
of drink, boasted of his part in the "Weida" Hotel
case, and defied either the police of the International
Settlement or French Concession to arrest him as he
had become a Japanese subject and had been granted a

The informer, employed by C.I in this case,

During the morning of the 17th.March, 1939,

With further reference to the man, Yeong Chien

Statement of TSEU YAH VUNG (周毓文); 30, M/Lawyer,
Taken at C. 1 on March 16, 1939.

My name is Tseu Yah Vung, aged 30, native of Changchow,
married, lawyer, residing at House 3, Lane 642, Chengtu Road.

On the early morning of 8.3.39 (6 a.m.) police visited
my house and placed me under arrest. I was then taken to Crime
Branch HQ's, S.M.P. wherefrom I was handed over at 6.30 p.m.
into the custody of the Japanese Gendarmerie, who brought me to
their headquarters at Hongkew for questioning, after which I
was detained in a cell together with 8 or 9 others, amongst
whom there were 2 Japanese and one Cantonese, the latter having
a blue scar on the face. Shortly afterwards, I began talking to
the Cantonese, enquiring the reason of his detention and how
he had received the wound on his face. After some moments'
hesitation, he informed me that the blue scar on his face was
his birth mark, and that he had been arrested in the following
manner :-

He stated that on the 6.3.39, in order to negotiate a
certain business, a foreigner accompanied him to Room 309 of
the Weida Hotel on Ave. Joffre, F. C. to interview one named
"Wong". Shortly after arrival in the Weida Hotel, Wong, the
foreigner and the Cantonese boarded the foreigner's car which
was waiting outside, proceeding to negotiate the business
somewhere else. However, on reaching a spot on Hart Road, the
car was stopped by a party of men, who at once placed them
under arrest.

He spoke in a half Cantonese and half Shanghai dialect,
and I experienced great difficulty in learning the foregoing
facts from him.

Prior to my being handed back to the S.M.P. I was warned
by the Japanese officers in Hongkew, that I should by no means
divulge anything which I had learned during my detention in Hong-
kew. Before I was brought away, however, the Cantonese also
pages.zh:
周毓文（TSEU YAH VUNG）的陈述；30 岁，男/律师，
1939 年 3 月 16 日于刑事调查处（C. 1）录取。

我叫周毓文，30 岁，常州人，已婚，律师，住成都路 642 弄 3 号。

1939 年 3 月 8 日凌晨（上午 6 点），警察来到我家并将我逮捕。随后我被带到工部局警务处刑事总部，下午 6:30 被移交给日本宪兵队，他们将我带到虹口总部进行讯问，之后我与另外 8 或 9 人一起被关押在一间牢房里，其中包括 2 名日本人和 1 名广东人，后者脸上有一块蓝色疤痕。不久后，我开始与这名广东人交谈，询问他被拘留的原因以及脸上的伤是如何造成的。犹豫片刻后，他告诉我，脸上的蓝色疤痕是他的胎记，他是以下述方式被捕的：

他说，1939 年 3 月 6 日，为了洽谈某项业务，一名外国人陪他前往法租界霞飞路（Ave. Joffre）维达饭店（Weida Hotel）309 室，去见一名叫“黄”的人。到达维达饭店后不久，黄、外国人和这名广东人登上了等在门外的外国人的汽车，前往别处洽谈业务。然而，当车到达哈特路（Hart Road）某处时，被一群人拦下，并立即将他们逮捕。

他说话夹杂着一半广东话和一半上海话，我从他那里了解上述事实时遇到了很大困难。

在我被移交给工部局警务处之前，虹口的日本军官警告我，绝不得泄露我在虹口拘留期间获悉的任何内容。然而，在我被带走之前，这名广东人也

pages.en:
(2)

requested that what he had told me should be kept secret.

During my detention in Hongkew, I also met Yoong Chien
Toon; in the cells. As far as I have learned, Yoong was arrested
at the same time with the Cantonese, whose name was "Wong", a man
of about 5'4", slim build, dark complexion, foreign clothes and
wearing a blue scar which almost covered half of his left face.
Wong was supposed to be employed by the accounts office of the
Metropole Ball Room and his residence was located at the An Loh
Faung, near the Corner of Gordon and Bubbling Well Roads.

This is the truth.

Signed                      TSEU YAH VUNG.
pages.zh:
(2)

请求我对他告诉我的事情保密。

在虹口拘留期间，我还在牢房里遇到了熊剑东（Yoong Chien Toon）。据我所知，熊是与那名名叫“黄”的广东人同时被捕的，该人身高约 5 英尺 4 英寸，身材瘦削，肤色黝黑，穿着西式服装，左脸近一半覆盖着蓝色疤痕。黄据说受雇于大都会舞厅（Metropole Ball Room）的会计室，住址位于戈登路（Gordon Road）与静安寺路（Bubbling Well Roads）转角附近的安乐坊（An Loh Faung）。

以上属实。

签名                      周毓文

CONFIDENTIAL

On the 9th March 1939, the undersigned
obtained information to the effect that Rabin had
brought about the arrest by the Japanese Secret Service
of two male Chinese, who had met him by appointment at
the "Weida" Hotel, Avenue Joffre, French Concession,
during the evening of the 6th March 1939 whilst
ostensibly negotiating an arms deal. No information
was obtained to substantiate this until the afternoon
of the 13th March 1939, when the undersigned and D.S.I.
Crighton made enquiries at French Police Headquarters.
It was then learned that investigations had already been
made into this case by D.S.I. Tilton, attached to B'Well.

The file B'Well Misc. 116/39, relating to
these enquiries, was passed to C.D.I. Grubb, by the D. C.
(Crime) the same afternoon. Briefly, from perusal of
this file it has been learned that the allegations made
against Rabin are apparently true, but whether the crime
originated in the Settlement or French Concession is a
matter for conjecture up to the present moment. If it is
deemed that the crime was planned in the Settlement, one
of the abducted men being a resident, then, instructions
are respectfully requested as to whether this Branch or
B'Well Detectives should proceed with the investigations
with a view to bringing about the arrest of Rabin.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
（批：FILE / d.R. / 14/3）

1939 年 3 月 9 日，签署人获得情报，称拉宾导致两名中国男子被日本特务机关逮捕，这两人于 1939 年 3 月 6 日晚在法租界霞飞路“维达”饭店与拉宾会面，表面上是洽谈军火交易。直到 1939 年 3 月 13 日下午，签署人与克里顿副督察（D.S.I. Crighton）在法国警察总部进行调查时，才获得证实这一情况的资料。当时获悉，隶属于 B'Well 的蒂尔顿副督察（D.S.I. Tilton）已经对此案进行了调查。

涉及这些调查的 B'Well 杂项 116/39 号档案，于当天下午由刑事副处长转交给格鲁布首席侦探督察（C.D.I. Grubb）。简而言之，通过查阅该档案得知，针对拉宾的指控显然属实，但犯罪起源于租界还是法租界，截至目前仍属推测。如果认为犯罪是在租界策划的，且被绑架者之一为居民，则谨请示指令，究竟是由本处还是由 B'Well 侦探继续进行调查，以便逮捕拉宾。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处）
（批：归档 / d.R. / 14/3）

The informer, who is working with the
investigating officers attached to this branch, visited
Rabin in his flat, situated at Apartment No. 611, The
Broadway Mansions, at 9 a.m. March 13th, 1939. Rabin
who was performing his ablutions in the bathroom, left
the informer alone in the drawing room. Glancing over
a writing desk he noticed that Rabin had noted on a date
block an appointment with Colonel Agaki, Chief of the
Intelligence Service, for 10 a.m. that morning. He also
noticed that an auto. pistol was lying in a half opened
drawer. Coming out of the bathroom, Rabin was informed
that D.I. Chu Shou Ling, who is acting as the purchaser
for a consignment of Mauser pistols, insisted that the
guns be delivered to an address which he would designate
and that he on no account would agree to any other
proposal as to accompanying Rabin or any other
individual to unknown addresses. Rabin then suggested
that Chu should meet him that evening in the lounge of
the "Cathay" Hotel, where they could talk over the
proposed transaction. On this information being conveyed
to C.B.I. Smith and the undersigned, the proposal was
vetoed on the grounds that it would be unwise to
jeopardise the safety of D.I. Chu, as it is more than
probable that Rabin intends to deal with him in the same
pages.zh:
- 2 -

与本处调查人员合作的线人，于 1939 年 3 月 13 日上午 9 点，在百老汇大厦（The Broadway Mansions）611 室公寓拜访了拉宾。拉宾当时正在浴室洗漱，将线人独自留在客厅。线人扫视书桌时，注意到拉宾在日期牌上记下了当天上午 10 点与情报处处长阿加基上校（Colonel Agaki）的约会。他还注意到一把自动手枪放在半开的抽屉里。拉宾从浴室出来后，线人告知他，充当毛瑟手枪批次购买者的朱守灵探员（D.I. Chu Shou Ling）坚持要求将枪支交付至他指定的地址，并且他绝不会同意陪同拉宾或任何其他个人前往未知地址的任何其他提议。拉宾随后建议朱当晚在“华懋”饭店（Cathay Hotel）的大堂与他见面，以便商谈拟议的交易。将此信息传达给史密斯首席侦探督察（C.B.I. Smith）和签署人后，该提议被否决，理由是危及朱守灵探员的安全是不明智的，因为拉宾极有可能以与

way as the two men abducted after the meeting at the
"Weida" Hotel.
Wane's
From perusal of D.S. Wafi's report it is
now apparent that the individual known to our informer
as "Mr. George", of No. 18, Lane 24, North Haining Road,
is none other than George Hoshinoya of the Japanese
Secret Service. It is also now very evident that the
alleged arms deal is nothing more than a ruse to entice
Chinese Guerilla leaders to come out into the open so
that they fall an easy prey to the Japanese authorities.
In view of this, I would respectfully suggest in order to
protect D.I. Chm Shou Ling that all further negotiations
be broken off, unless the arrest of Rubin is desired.
(As George Hoshinoya is alleged to be a Canadian (British
subject) I would suggest that this be brought to the
notice of H.B.M.'s Consulate.

that he has a

M.C.）

ABDUCTION OF A MALE CHINESE BY JAPANESE
IN CIVILIAN CLOTHING
========================================

Further information obtained by D.S.I. Tilton and
D.S.I. Golobkoff indicates that Nathan Rabin is connected
with Mr. R.W. Meyer (American). The latter is well known
in Shanghai and has a record at the American Consulate
General. He opened an office about October 1938 at Room
205, Hamilton House where he carries on a business under
the name of the "Far Eastern Trading Syndicate."

The nature of the business is reputed to be shady
transactions, connected with Japanese and involving
Chinese who are contacted or induced in various ways
to put up money to purchase arms for guerillas following
which they are turned over to Japanese and the money
"confiscated".

D.S.I. Tilton

一名华籍男子被身着便服的日本人绑架
===

警探副督察蒂尔顿（Tilton）和警探副督察戈洛布科夫（Golobkoff）获得的进一步情报显示，内森·拉宾（Nathan Rabin）与美国人 R.W. 迈耶（R.W. Meyer）先生有关联。后者在上海颇有名气，在美国总领事馆留有档案。他于1938年10月左右在汉密尔顿大楼（Hamilton House）205室开设办事处，以“远东贸易辛迪加”（Far Eastern Trading Syndicate）的名义开展业务。

据称，该业务的性质涉及 shady transactions（可疑交易），与日本人有关联，并牵涉到通过多种方式接触或诱使华人出资购买供游击队使用的武器，随后这些人被移交给日本人，资金则被“没收”。

At 11 a.m. Saturday, March 11, 1939 Mr. O.Boisserée (British), Coal Merchant, residing Flat 3, 1933 B'well Road, trading as U.S. Oriental Trading Co., office 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, came to the Station and reported that he was approached by a Mr. Wong Tsun Wei(黃廷煒), age 40, Cantonese, broker, who resided at No.37 Sun Avenue, on Friday, March 3, 1939 to go with Wong as a witness concerning a deal he intended to transact. No. 33, Lane No. 180, Tifeng Road. Whether this person
is one named Alex Leo Gutterman (Z.943 & C.47/35) who
has a previous conviction cannot at the present be
ascertained.

Following the receipt of this information
it was arranged that Mr. Jellinek should introduce Det.
Inspr. Chm Shou Ling, attached to this branch, to Rabin
as a prospective buyer at a meeting which he would
arrange for the following day at the "Chocolate Shop",
Nanking Road.

At 9.45 a.m. March 2nd, 1939, Mr. Jellinek
introduced D.I. Chm to Rabin. D.I. Chm, representing
pages.zh:
- 5 -

此人，耶利内克先生（Mr. Jellinek）被警告要提防拉宾（Rabin）。
当被问及他是否认为这是一桩虚假交易时，戈夫（Goff）表示他与此事毫无瓜葛，无法断定其真假，但他对拉宾非常怀疑。不过，他能够陈述的是，布兰（Bran，存疑）曾向他保证，他见过一些待售的枪支。

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.I.）格鲁布（Grubb）向美国总领事馆查询后查明，拉宾并非美国公民。

进一步查询获悉，拉宾提供的私人电话号码 23163，登记在提丰路（Tifeng Road）180 弄 33 号的桑迪·古特曼（Sandy Gutterman）名下。目前尚无法确定此人是否为曾有前科的亚历克斯·里奥·古特曼（Alex Leo Gutterman，档案号 Z.943 & C.47/35）。

收到此信息后，当局安排耶利内克先生将隶属于本处的侦探督察陈守灵（Det. Inspr. Chm Shou Ling）作为潜在买家介绍给拉宾，会面由耶利内克安排在次日于南京路“巧克力店”（Chocolate Shop）举行。

1939 年 3 月 2 日上午 9 时 45 分，耶利内克先生将侦探督察陈（D.I. Chm）介绍给拉宾。侦探督察陈代表

pages.en:
- 6 -

himself as a "middleman", discussed the conditions to
purchase the second described consignment of arms,
consisting of Mauser pistols. Rabin then stated that
the pistols did not actually belong to him, and that
he was only acting as a broker for the owner, who
resided in the French Concession. He stipulated that
the purchase money should be delivered by D.I. Chu to
an address in the French Concession, to which he would
lead him, and where if everything was satisfactory the
arms would be delivered. D.I. Chu objected to the deal
being consummated in the French Concession, and proposed
the International Settlement, claiming that it would be
much safer for him under this condition. This
terminated the interview, but it was agreed to meet the
following morning at the same place. At the time
appointed Mr. Jellinek and D.I. Chu again met Rabin.
The latter stated that the seller had agreed to the
stipulation made by the purchaser to the effect that
the sale should be effected in the International
Settlement. The seller, however, stipulated that the
money, $12,000.00 in notes, should be produced for
inspection prior to the delivery of the arms. This,
D.I. Chu protested, would leave the buyer open to either
being held up and robbed or by some other means
pages.zh:
- 6 -

自称是“中间人”，商谈购买第二批所述军火的条件，该批军火由毛瑟手枪组成。拉宾（Rabin）随后声明，这些手枪实际上并不属于他，他只是代表居住在法租界的货主行事，充当经纪人。他规定，购货款应由朱巡长（D.I. Chu）送至法租界的一个地址，他将带朱巡长前往该处，若一切顺利，将在该处交付军火。朱巡长反对在法租界完成交易，并提议在国际公共租界进行，声称在此条件下对他而言更为安全。此次面谈至此结束，但双方约定次日上午在同一地点再次会面。在约定时间，杰利内克先生（Mr. Jellinek）和朱巡长再次会见了拉宾。后者表示，卖方已同意买方提出的规定，即交易应在国际公共租界进行。然而，卖方规定，在交付军火之前，必须先出示现款12,000.00美元以供查验。对此，朱巡长提出抗议，认为这将使买方面临被持械抢劫或以其他手段

pages.en:
- 7 -

defrauded. Rabin then stated that he would have to
leave the matter in abeyance until he had consulted
the owner on this point. The interview was then
concluded, but it was arranged that a further meeting
should take place at the same place that afternoon at
5.45 p.m.

At 4 p.m. the same day, Mr. Jellinek called
on C.D.I. Grubb, and during the ensuing conversation
mentioned that Rabin had been associated with Rudolph
Mayer (American), but that he was, as far as he knew,
not connected with this alleged arms deal.

At 5.45 p.m. D.I. Gin and Mr. Jellinek met
Rabin at the "Chocolate Shop". On this occasion Rabin
suggested that in order to allay D.I. Gin's suspicions,
that he should provide himself with bodyguards. They
should proceed by motorcar to an address, to which he
would lead them. On arrival the owner of the pistols
would inspect the money whilst they were in the car.
They would then proceed to inspect the pistols, after
which the transfer would be effected. This concluded
the meeting, but they arranged to meet again at 10.35
a.m. on the 4th March 1936. At the appointed time, they
again met, when Rabin was informed by D.I. Gin that the
suggestion made the previous day was unacceptable to the
pages.zh:
- 7 -

诈骗的风险。拉宾随后表示，在他就此点咨询货主之前，此事只能暂时搁置。面谈随即结束，但约定于当日下午5时45分在同一地点再次会面。

同日下午4时，杰利内克先生拜访了副侦探督察格拉布（C.D.I. Grubb），并在随后的谈话中提到，拉宾曾与鲁道夫·迈耶（Rudolph Mayer，美国人）有往来，但据他所知，拉宾与这起所谓的军火交易并无关联。

下午5时45分，金巡长（D.I. Gin）和杰利内克先生在“巧克力店”（Chocolate Shop）会见了拉宾。在此次会面中，拉宾建议，为了消除金巡长的疑虑，他应自带保镖。他们应乘车前往一个地址，由他带路。到达后，手枪货主将在车内查验现款。随后他们将去查验手枪，之后完成移交。此次会面结束，但双方约定于1936年3月4日上午10时35分再次会面。在约定时间，他们再次见面，此时金巡长告知拉宾，前一天提出的建议不被买

pages.en:
- 8 -

buyer. D.I. Chu stipulated that the arms be delivered
to a place to be designated by him, but this was
refused. A further meeting took place at 5.30 p.m.
March 4th, 1939, but as no satisfactory arrangement
could be arrived at no further meetings were arranged.
According to Mr. Jellinek, Rabin is still
anxious to proceed with the business, and as soon as
he makes any further suggestions he will communicate
with the undersigned.
Whether or not Rabin is trying to negotiate
a genuine arms deal cannot at the moment be ascertained,
but if he is not, he is either planning to defraud any
prospective buyer, or is merely in the employ of the
Japanese Secret Service as an Agent Provocateur in
arresting leaders of Guerilla Units who might want to
purchase arms for their various units engaged in anti-
Japanese activities.
In a conversation with D.S.I. Rhind,
Officer 1/c **〔此处转录不清〕**, the undersigned learned that
Rabin is at the moment living at the Nifong Road
address with George Leonoff (Russian), whilst Sandy
Guttmann, who is listed as the subscriber to the
telephone at that address, is at present in the
Philippine Island, where he fled after having been
pages.zh:
- 8 -

方接受。朱巡长规定，军火应交付至由他指定的地点，但这一要求被拒绝。1939年3月4日下午5时30分又进行了一次会面，但由于未能达成令人满意的安排，未再安排后续会面。据杰利内克先生称，拉宾仍急于推进这笔生意，一旦他提出任何进一步建议，他将与具名者联系。

目前尚无法确定拉宾是否试图洽谈一笔真实的军火交易，但如果不是，他要么是在策划诈骗任何潜在买家，要么仅仅是受雇于日本特务机关，作为挑衅代理人（Agent Provocateur），逮捕那些可能想为其从事反日活动的各游击队单位购买军火的游击队领导人。

在与副侦探督察莱因德（D.S.I. Rhind，**〔此处转录不清〕**主管警官）的谈话中，具名者获悉，拉宾目前与乔治·列昂诺夫（George Leonoff，俄国人）住在尼丰路（Nifong Road）的地址，而登记为该地址电话用户的桑迪·古特曼（Sandy Guttmann）目前在菲律宾群岛，他在卷入一桩可疑的毒品交易后逃往该地。

pages.en:
- 9 -

concerned in a shady deal concerning narcotics. D.S.I.
Rhind was also able to inform the undersigned that
Kuwahata, who at the moment is also absent from
Shanghai, is a notorious narcotic trafficker, and some
time ago was concerned in selling drugs to Italian
Officers of the M.V. "Conte Biancamano".

On being shown a photograph of Rubin by
Chief Inspr. Hall of the Traffic Dept., the undersigned
recognised him as a man known as Nathan, who at one time
conducted an Orchestra at Ciro's and the Little Club.
This man is a low type of Jew, wholly unscrupulous and
just the person to commit a particularly mean type of
fraud. In view of this, it would appear that the whole
thing is nothing more than an attempted fraud or
possibly he is being employed by the Japanese to locate
leaders of Guerilla troops.

During the afternoon of the 8th March 1938,
Mr. Jellinek informed C.D.I. Crubb and the undersigned
that he had received a telephone message from Rubin
asking him to call at House No. 18, Lane 24, North
Haining Road. As Mr. Jellinek knew that this address
was being used by the Japanese Secret Service, he asked
if it was advisable for him to go or not. C.D.I. Crubb
and the undersigned advised him not to go, but to ring
up this address and ask Rubin to meet him on Nanking Road.
pages.zh:
- 9 -

副侦探督察莱因德还告知具名者，桑原（Kuwahata，音译）目前也不在上海，他是一个臭名昭著的毒品贩子，前一段时间曾参与向意大利籍“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（M.V. "Conte Biancamano"）轮船的军官出售毒品。

当交通部霍尔总督察（Chief Inspr. Hall）向具名者展示鲁宾（Rubin）的照片时，具名者认出此人是一个名叫纳坦（Nathan）的人，他曾在西罗餐厅（Ciro's）和小俱乐部（Little Club）经营一支乐队。此人是一个卑劣的犹太人，毫无道德底线，正是那种会实施特别卑鄙欺诈行为的人。鉴于此，整件事似乎不过是一次未遂的诈骗，或者他可能是被日本人雇佣来定位游击队领导人的。

1938年3月8日下午，杰利内克先生告知副侦探督察克拉布（C.D.I. Crubb）和具名者，他接到鲁宾的电话留言，要求他去海宁北路24弄18号。由于杰利内克先生知道该地址正被日本特务机关使用，他询问是否适宜前往。副侦探督察克拉布和具名者建议他不要前往，而是致电该地址，要求鲁宾在南京路与他会面。

pages.en:
- 10 -

He did as he was instructed and was told by "George"
that Rabin was not there.

Mr. Jellinek was able to inform the under-
signed that "George" was a well educated Japanese, who
appeared to hold a high position in the Japanese Secret
Service, as he frequently travelled between Shanghai
and Tokyo by plane.

Later in the day, Mr. Jellinek informed the
undersigned that following the receipt of a further
telephone message, he had met Rabin outside House No.
18, Lane No. 24, North Haining Road. Rabin stated
that he had learned from a friend in the U. S. Consulate
that the Police were making enquiries about him, and
in consequence he had removed to North Haining Road
until the matter had blown over. Mr. Jellinek assured
him that he knew nothing of the matter, and Rabin then
stated that he suspected that Goff had given information
to the Police.

Efforts are now being made to ascertain more
details regarding the activities of Rabin, which will be
reported on at a later date.

M. C. Flower
D. I.
pages.zh:
- 10 -

他照指示行事，但被告知“乔治”说拉宾不在那里。

杰利内克先生能够告知具名者，“乔治”是一位受过良好教育的日本人，似乎在日本特务机关中担任高级职位，因为他经常乘飞机往返于上海和东京之间。

当天晚些时候，杰利内克先生告知具名者，在收到另一通电话留言后，他在海宁北路24弄18号门外会见了拉宾。拉宾表示，他从美国领事馆的一位朋友那里得知警方正在调查他，因此他搬到了海宁北路，直到风头过去。杰利内克先生向他保证自己对此事一无所知，拉宾随后表示，他怀疑戈夫（Goff）向警方提供了情报。

目前正在努力查明有关拉宾活动的更多细节，并将稍后报告。

M. C. Flower
侦探督察（D. I.）

2.

ABDUCTION OF A MALE CHINESE BY JAPANESE IN CIVILIAN
CLOTHING.

At 4p.m. 7/3/39 D.S. Nagamune interviewed Sgt.
Matsumoto at the Japanese Consulate, and learned that
S.M.C. Lic. Plates No. 5601 were attached to a two-
seater Citroen Coupe parked in Lane 24 Haining Road.
It was stated that this car had not been used since
January 1939. Examination of the car at 5p.m. 7/3/39
by D.B. Nagamune showed that the car had not been used
for some considerable period; the tyres were flat, the
inside floorboards were missing and the upholstery was
covered with a thick layer of dirt.

At 9.30a.m. 8/3/39 on the instructions of D.I.
Tabrum, Sen. Det. i/c., D.S. Fare and D.S. Nagamune
proceeded to Lane 18 Haining Road and re-inspected the
car. The details given above were found correct and
in addition the radiator appeared to be empty and the
shanks of the license plate bolts bore a covering of
bright red rust and the nuts were screwed up tightly.

Enquiries at the Traffic Office concerning the
use of the S.M.C. Licence Plates produced the following:-
S.M.C. License Plates No. 5601 were returned
to the Traffic Office on 6/7/38 by Mr. E. Kalen, Esq.
Vice Consul for Austria.

一名中国男子被便衣日本人绑架案。

1939年3月7日下午4时，永宗（Nagamune，音译）侦探副督察在日本领事馆讯问了松本（Matsumoto）警佐，获悉工部局车牌号为5601的车牌挂在一辆停在海宁北路24弄的双座雪铁龙轿跑车上。据称，该车自1939年1月以来未曾使用。1939年3月7日下午5时，永宗侦探副督察对该车进行检查，发现该车已有相当长一段时间未使用；轮胎瘪气，内部地板缺失，内饰覆盖着厚厚一层灰尘。

1939年3月8日上午9时30分，根据首席侦探督察塔布鲁姆（D.I. Tabrum，主管高级侦探）的指令，费尔侦探副督察（D.S. Fare）和永宗侦探副督察前往海宁北路18弄，重新检查了该车。上述细节经核实无误，此外散热器似乎是空的，车牌螺栓杆上覆盖着鲜红的铁锈，螺母拧得很紧。

Misc. No. 116/39.

2/sheet 2.

On 26/7/38 the plates were issued to Yoshinobu
Kawahata in respect of his "Opel" m/car which is a
twelve h.p., four cylinder, four seater open touring
car, Engine No. M.835164. The predominant colour
is green with green disc wheels, and a luggage carrier
is fitted in the trunk. The application was renewed
on 8/2/39.

A search of the files failed to show that Y.
Kawahata has a driving permit, permanent or temporary.
(Names bearing some similarity in spelling were also
inspected). However, it was found that a Japanese
named George Hoshinoya, S.M.C. Permit "E" 610, was
passed out at Muirhead Road Depot on 28/9/38 as being
a capable driver. The car used was an "Opel" S.M.C.
No. 5601. In respect of this a letter attached to
the test slip states:-

Shanghai, 28 Sept, 1938.

To whom it may concern.

This is to certify that the bearer G.
Hoshinoya is authorised to utilise my car No. 5601
for his driving test and also henceforth, for any
other purposes.
(Sd.) Y. Kawahata.

This file gives the present address of G.
Hoshinoya as Lane 24/18 Haining Road, and business
address as 202 Ewa Building, Kinkiang Road. Another
pages.zh:
杂项编号 116/39。

2/第2页。

1938年7月26日，该车牌发给川畑吉信（Yoshinobu Kawahata，音译），用于其“欧宝”（Opel）机动车，该车为12马力、四缸、四座敞篷旅行车，发动机号M.835164。主色调为绿色，配有绿色盘式车轮，后备箱装有行李架。申请于1939年2月8日续期。

查阅档案未发现Y. Kawahata拥有永久或临时驾驶执照。（也检查了拼写相近的名字）。然而，发现一名叫星野乔治（George Hoshinoya，音译）的日本人，持有工部局“E”类许可证610号，于1938年9月28日在缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road）车场通过考核，被认定为合格驾驶员。所用车辆为“欧宝”牌，工部局车牌号5601。对此，附在测试单上的一封信函写明：

上海，1938年9月28日。

致有关人士。

兹证明持证人G. Hoshinoya获准使用我的5601号汽车进行驾驶测试，并此后用于任何其他目的。
（签名）Y. Kawahata。

该档案显示G. Hoshinoya的现住址为海宁北路24弄18号，营业地址为九江路爱华大楼（Ewa Building）202室。另一个

pages.en:
Misc. No. 116/38.

2/sheet 3.

business address given in connection with the car
registration is No. 21 (7) Capital Building, Museum
Road.

An interesting discovery in the Traffic Office
files is that Tatsuo Kawahata, the son of Yoshinobu
Kawahata, was the licensee of a private m/car 4902.
This car, now detained by the Japanese Consular Police,
was used by Chinese for the transportation of narcotics
during June/July 1938. The Chinese were dealt with
by the S.P.Office, but Tatsuo Kawahata was absent from
Shanghai on a trip to Nanking and has not been heard of
since. According to D.S. Hagmann, Tatsuo Kawahata is,
by common gossip, said to have been ambushed by
guerrillas whilst on his journey to Nanking.

D. S.
D.S. Hagmann.

Sen. 1/8.

D.D.O. "B".

与车辆登记相关的营业地址是博物馆路首都大楼（Capital Building）21号（7室）。

Abduction of a male Chinese by Japanese
in civilian clothing.

At 8.45 p.m. 6-3-39 C.P.C. 2018 (traffic duty
at the intersection of Avenue and Seymour Roads)
and Mr. S. Abolnik who resides at Apt. C.2, No.1248
Rue Lafayette, came to Bubbling Well Station and
made the following report:-

At about 8.35 p.m. 6-3-39 an unidentified m/car
was proceeding on Avenue Road from west to east with
another m/car of the "Nash" or "Buick" type S.M.C.
No.5601, following behind. When about five yards west
of Seymour Road m/car S.M.C. No.5601 stopped quickly
with the brakes screeching. Immediately following
this a Chinese was heard to cry out in pain as, or
after four Japanese in civilian clothes dismounted from
the car, picked up a male Chinese from the roadway
and bundled him into the car. C.P.C. 2018 observed
that the Chinese was bleeding profusely from the
head, and Mr. Abolnik noticed that he was wearing
some sort of dark long gown. The car was stationary
only a very short period, a matter of seconds, before
it was driven away eastward.

Neither C.P.C. 2018 nor Mr. Abolnik saw pistols
or other weapons .

一名中国男子被便衣日本人绑架案。

1939年3月6日晚上8时45分，巡捕2018号（在爱文义路和西摩路交叉口执行交通勤务）和居住在拉斐德路1248号C.2公寓的S. Abolnik先生来到静安寺捕房，作出如下报告：

1939年3月6日晚上8时35分左右，一辆不明机动车沿爱文义路自西向东行驶，另一辆“纳什”（Nash）或“别克”（Buick）类型的机动车紧随其后，车牌为工部局5601号。当行驶至西摩路以西约五码处时，5601号机动车急刹车停下，发出刺耳的声音。紧接着，听到一名中国人痛苦地叫喊，三四名便衣日本人下车，从路面上抱起一名中国男子，将其塞进车内。巡捕2018号观察到该中国男子头部大量出血，Abolnik先生注意到他穿着某种深色长袍。该车仅静止了极短的时间，不过几秒钟，便向东驶离。

巡捕2018号和Abolnik先生均未看到手枪或其他武器。

pages.en:
Misc. No. 11L/39

1 (Sheet 2)

The intersection where this occurrence happened
is purely residential, there being no shops or alleys
where additional witnesses might be found for many yards.

On checking the registration of private m/car 5601,
it was found to be in the name of Yoshinobu Kuwahata
who lives at **〔此处转录不清〕** 24, House 18 Maining Road.

D.S. Magamure and the undersigned proceeded to
Hongkew Station and learned that no report of the
occurrence been made there (should it have been a
peculiar accident).

The same detectives then proceeded to the offices
of the Japanese Consular Police for assistance to visit
the home of Yoshinobu Kuwahata. Japanese Consular
Sgt. Matsumoto refused to give assistance and stated
that his department would fully investigate the case
and inform Bubbling Well Station of the result on
7-3-39.

No enquiries have been made by the public con-
cerning the missing Chinese and no hospital reports
have been received.

Should this occurrence be an abduction it must
have been carefully planned with the car waiting nearby
with the engine running; otherwise meeting the victim
in the middle of the road suggests a fortuitous
coincidence.

杂项编号 11L/39

1（第2页）

事发路口纯属居民区，周围数码内没有商店或弄堂，无法找到更多目击者。

经查证私人机动车5601号的登记情况，发现车主为川畑吉信（Yoshinobu Kuwahata，音译），居住在海宁北路**〔此处转录不清〕**24弄18号。

Magamure侦探副督察（音译）和具名者前往虹口捕房，获悉该处未收到关于此事件的报告（假如这是一起特殊事故的话）。

随后，这两名侦探前往日本领事警察办事处寻求协助，以便访问川畑吉信的住所。日本领事警佐松本拒绝提供协助，并表示其部门将全面调查此案，并于1939年3月7日将结果通知静安寺捕房。

公众未就失踪的中国男子进行任何查询，也未收到医院报告。

如果此事件确系绑架，则必然是经过精心策划的，车辆就在附近等候且引擎处于运转状态；否则，在路中间遇到受害者表明这是一种偶然的巧合。
